description: A four-panel set of SEM-EBSD phase maps of Fe–20Mn–9Al–3Cr-xC low-density steel strips, panels labelled (a)–(d) at top left, each covering the same field size and carrying a white 50 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner. All panels show a polygonal microstructure in which grains are outlined by dark boundary lines; two phases are colour-coded — red (ferrite) and grey (austenite), per the caption ("The red and gray contrasts indicate ferrite and austenite, respectively"). (a) 0.8C contains abundant, coarse, mostly equiaxed red ferrite patches distributed through the grey austenite. In (b) 1.0C the red fraction is already reduced and the red regions become finer and more elongated. (c) 1.2C shows sparse red ferrite mostly as thin lenticular/lath-like features and strings along grain boundaries within large grey austenite grains. (d) 1.4C retains only a few red laths, essentially confined to grain-boundary regions, the matrix being predominantly grey austenite. No phase fractions, colour key or legend bar are printed on the panels, so the quantitative ferrite contents are taken from the caption/citation, not read from the pixels.

subfigures.description: SEM-EBSD phase map of the 0.8C steel strip (Fe–20Mn–9Al–3Cr–0.8C), 50 µm scale bar: abundant coarse, largely equiaxed red ferrite regions dispersed in the grey austenite matrix, grains outlined by dark boundaries.
Phase map of the 1.0C steel strip, 50 µm scale bar: grey austenite matrix with a visibly smaller red ferrite fraction than (a), the red regions finer and more elongated.
Phase map of the 1.2C steel strip, 50 µm scale bar: large grey austenite grains containing only sparse red ferrite, appearing as thin lath-like/stringer features preferentially at boundaries.
Phase map of the 1.4C steel strip, 50 µm scale bar: predominantly grey austenite with only a few isolated red ferrite laths, mostly near grain boundaries.

observations.observation: The figure is a set of four SEM-EBSD phase maps labelled (a)–(d), each with a white 50 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner.
Red regions are most abundant and coarsest in (a) and become progressively sparser through (b) and (c) to only a few isolated laths in (d).
In (a) and (b) the red ferrite appears as relatively equiaxed patches, whereas in (c) and (d) it appears as thin elongated lath/lenticular features located mainly along grain boundaries.
Dark continuous lines outline polygonal grains in all four panels, indicating high-angle grain boundaries between the phase regions.
No colour key, legend bar or printed phase-fraction value appears inside any panel; the red/grey phase assignment is not annotated in the pixels.
The caption states that the red and gray contrasts indicate ferrite and austenite, respectively.
The caption identifies the four strips as Fe–20Mn–9Al–3Cr-xC with x = 0.8C (a), 1.0C (b), 1.2C (c) and 1.4C (d), i.e. differing only in C content.
The citing text states that as C increased from 0.8 wt% to 1.4 wt%, the volume fraction of ferrite decreased from 36 vol% to 4 vol%, which is the quantitative reading of the trend visible in (a)–(d).
The citing text states that the samples were produced by the centrifugal casting method.
The citing text states that precipitation of the DO3 phase in the ferrite decreased as C content increased.
The citing text states that the yield strength rose from 680 MPa at 0.8 wt% C to 992 MPa at 1.4 wt% C, and that elongation remained 33% or more.
The citing text states that dispersion strengthening from κ-carbides in austenite increased from 36.3 MPa (0.8 wt% C) to 409.4 MPa (1.4 wt% C).
